newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-API crude to build, but downswing seen.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-API crude to build, but downswing seen.

text.p: A significant build in crude stocks is widely-expected by traders in Tuesday's oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API), but some dealers say this could be one of the last big builds in crude stocks for a while.

"Tonight's report could be extremely important. We could have a bigger-than-expected build tonight, which would be like the last big heave before a sustained refinery (run) upswing," said William Brown, president of New York trading firm W.H. Brown & Co.
A consensus of trader estimates pegged the crude build at 3.5 million barrels, with a traditionally disparate estimate range for crude of between flat and up six million barrels.
Tuesday's API data reflects the week ended March 7.
Dealers said to certain extent the expected crude build has already been discounted by the market.
Indeed, the factors behind tonight's crude build are also what sent crude prices into contango for first time in two years Monday: low refinery operating rates and increased imports.

"I think we are going to have pretty hefty imports for the next four to five weeks," said Jim Ritterbusch, trader with Sweeeney Oil in Illinois, who, unlike Brown, is in the camp that believes tonight's build will be one of several consecutive builds yet to come.
This winter's heavy European refinery maintenance cut crude usage markedly there and sent crudes from abroad, particularly from West Africa, searching for a home.
A bevy of this foreign supply has since arrived in the U.S. Gulf just when U.S. refiners are in the tailend of their own maintenance season, dealers have said.

"There is nothing abnormal about these imports. The turning point will be when you see a pop in crude runs. That can happen in two weeks," said John Saucer, analyst with Smith Barney in Houston, who expects that big stock builds in crude could be nearing their end.

Not surprisingly, this week's API are expected to show refinery runs about steady with last week's low run rate of 88.6 percent. Last week's report also showed crude stocks were 5.2 million barrels above a year ago.
Gasoline stocks are seen steady to slightly lower while distillate stocks are seen showing a 1.6 million barrel draw.

"Demand should continue strong when runs are still pretty low," said one trader of gasoline. Gasoline's implied demand was a seasonally high 7.9 million barrels a day (bpd) for the week ended Ferbruary 28, and over eight million bpd the week before.
Distillate stocks, which include heating oil and diesel, usually decline this time of year as refiners steer away from distillate production due to the end of winter.
